basis: Vietnamese signal heads are commonly visible from both sides; a head placed on a road controls the lane travelling towards it on that road. The signal-to-approach mapping drawn by the owner is authoritative; it is not inferred from which way the visible face points.
note: An earlier suggestion by the assistant that a camera-facing head controls only traffic moving away from the camera was wrong for this context and is withdrawn.

configs_not_used.aicc22:v2: US source: signals are usually far-side and single-faced, so the visible heads control traffic moving away from the camera, while the drawn approach moves towards it. The owner asked to use it only if it follows the Vietnamese convention; it does not, so it is not activated.
